Hi Elena —

Quick answers to the items above:
- SCIM: We support SCIM 2.0 with incremental and full sync endpoints. Our default mapping includes email, givenName, familyName, displayName, and groups. We can accept custom attributes (businessUnit, costCenter); scim_mapping.csv in the attachment shows how to map them to attributes in our directory.
- Service accounts / keys: We prefer short-lived OAuth tokens exchanged via a service account + signed JWT flow. If you must use long-lived API keys we can accommodate under strict rotation policies, but recommend the rotating token approach integrated with your KMS. Documentation link in the playbook (page 4) shows the JWT exchange steps.
- IP allowlists: We support both per-org and per-workspace allowlists. For most bank integrations we recommend per-org allowlist at the edge plus per-workspace rules for staging. Include both prod and pre-prod CIDRs and tag them; we'll put prod on the stricter policy.

SAML specifics we need from you to finish our SP config:
- IdP entity ID and ACS URL
- Single Logout (SLO) endpoint (optional)
- x509 certificate (PEM) or IdP metadata XML (you can send metadata.xml)

Typical timeline: once we have signed SAML metadata and the SCIM owner confirmed, most orgs see end-to-end provisioning within 3 business days (config, test, and rollout to pilot). If there are custom attribute mappings or complicated group rules, plan for 5-7 business days. Procurement can count on the 3–7 business day window depending on customizations.

Cheers —
